mission: Y Combinator helps founders start companies through funding, advice, and a powerful alumni network.

featured.responsibilities: Build and iterate a startup during the YC batch, talk to users, ship product, and present at Demo Day with your co-founders.
featured.qualifications: A founding team (or strong solo case), a clear problem/solution thesis, and commitment to work on the company full-time if accepted. Bio/health startups are welcome when ready.

mission: Y Combinator funds and supports early-stage startups across industries, including bio and health.

featured.position: Role at a YC-backed startup (select a live job on the YC Jobs board)
featured.responsibilities: Join an early startup team to build product, run experiments, or support scientific/commercial work depending on the company posting.
featured.qualifications: Skills listed by the hiring startup (often full-stack, ML, biology, or ops). Filter the YC Jobs board for bio/health roles that match you.

mission: NSF I-Corps trains researchers to test commercial potential of deep science and engineering ideas.

featured.responsibilities: Complete customer-discovery interviews, test value propositions for a research-based idea, and report learning with your I-Corps team.
featured.qualifications: Typically an academic team (PI/entrepreneurial lead/mentor) with a deep-tech or life-science concept; eligibility depends on the Hub/Teams call.

mission: BioLabs provides shared lab infrastructure and community for early-stage biotech companies.

featured.position: Resident company / join a BioLabs site pathway
featured.responsibilities: Operate your early biotech company in shared lab space, follow site EH&S rules, and engage with the BioLabs founder community.
featured.qualifications: An incorporated (or forming) biotech startup needing lab access; scientific founders with a clear experimental plan are typical applicants.

mission: CDL is an objectives-based program for massively scalable science- and tech-based ventures.

featured.position: CDL venture participant (apply to an open stream)
featured.responsibilities: Set and hit commercialization objectives with CDL mentors, refine go-to-market and technical milestones, and engage in sessions throughout the program.
featured.qualifications: A scalable science/tech venture at a stage matching the stream; founding team committed to the CDL objectives process.

mission: Breakout backs scientific founders building transformative deep-tech and life-science companies.

featured.position: Breakout portfolio / program application path (when a call is open)
featured.responsibilities: Work with Breakout on company building for a scientific venture—diligence, milestones, and founder support as defined by the active program.
featured.qualifications: Scientific founders with a deep-tech or life-science thesis; check Breakout’s site for current application criteria.

mission: NIH SEED helps small businesses turn promising technologies into products that improve health.

featured.responsibilities: Prepare and submit an NIH small-business research proposal, execute the funded R&D plan, and report progress under NIH terms.
featured.qualifications: A qualifying small business with a health-related innovation; PI and company eligibility rules are defined in the current Omnibus/solicitation.

mission: IndieBio helps scientist-founders turn biology breakthroughs into companies through funding and lab support.

featured.responsibilities: If accepted, build the company in-program: experiments, customer discovery, and investor milestones with IndieBio mentors.
featured.qualifications: Scientist-founders with a biology-driven company idea; team commitment and ability to relocate/participate as required by the cohort.
